 Sports Shelton’s season best 43rd win moves him into Paris Masters quarterfinals 
 Jerome Pugmireap Published on :  06 Nov 2026, 9:25 pm 
 Copied 
 Follow Us Ben Shelton beat Arthur Rinderknech 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) for a season’s best 43rd win and a spot in the Paris Masters quarterfinals.
 The US Open runner-up next faces Number 12 Tommy Paul in an all-American contest. It will be their fifth career meeting, with the players on two wins each, and the first since 2024. “It’s been a long time since we’ve been on the court, but I’m looking forward to it,” Shelton said. “He’s in great form right now. A great player, a great friend.”
 Paul earlier beat Quentin Halys 7-6 (3), 6-4 in the third round to maintain an outside chance of clinching one of the two remaining spots for the Nov. 15-22 ATP Finals in Turin.
 “I’ve been rooting for him all year to make a push and make it to Turin,” said Shelton, who is among the six players already qualified. “It will be fireworks tomorrow.”
 Earlier, Carlos Alcaraz advanced after Matteo Berrettini withdrew from their third-round match because of an arm injury. The big-serving Italian did not specify which arm but said in an Instagram post that he has been in pain for a few days.
 The second-seeded Alcaraz’s quarterfinal opponent will be the winner of a match later Thursday between sixth-seeded Arthur Fils of France and No. 11 Taylor Fritz, who is also trying to reach the ATP Finals. A loss for Fritz later would qualify fellow American Frances Tiafoe.
 Another Frenchman got home fans on their feet even before Fils played, with Luca Van Assche beating Lorenzo Musetti 7-5, 3-6, 6-4 to reach his first-ever Masters quarterfinal.
 The Number 47-ranked Van Assche served out the match with a neat volley at the net on his first match point against Musetti, who has reached at least the quarterfinals at all four majors.
 After beating Novak Djokovic in the second round, qualifier Rinky Hijikata advanced with a 2-6, 6-3, 7-5 win over Tomas Etcheverry and plays Van Assche next.
